Subject: Request: APAC analytics partner - egress exception and SLA impact

Hi Kimberly,

Quick note from our ops team — we're planning a short pilot that sends telemetry and anonymized usage metrics to an APAC-based analytics partner (EdgeProbe Ltd) for a 30-day pilot starting next week. EdgeProbe is listed as a new subprocessor on your vendor portal but we couldn't find any details about cross-border egress for EU-origin traffic.

We need two things to sign off on the pilot:
- A current subprocessor manifest (full list) and explicit confirmation whether any EU PII or metadata would leave the EU/EEA in this pilot.
- Assessment of any SLA or credit implications if routing via EdgeProbe introduces additional latency or intermittent delivery issues for our customer-facing features.

Can you share the manifest and an estimated timeline? If there's a DPA addendum or an egress exception process we should follow, please point us to the docs. We need to present this to Security & Legal tonight.

Thanks,
Olivia

Hi Olivia — thanks for the heads up and the clear ask. We're triaging this now.

Short answer on process: we can support a limited pilot that routes specified telemetry to EdgeProbe, but it requires a scoped DPA addendum (explicit subprocessor clause + transfer safeguards) and a short security checklist before we allow EU-origin telemetry to egress. I can get you the manifest and a first-pass addendum by tomorrow EOD.

To speed internal scoping, could you confirm:
- Example production domain(s) where telemetry will be collected (so we can map routes).
- The specific data types you expect to forward (anonymized metrics, request timings, user-agent hashes, any identifiers?).

I'll loop in Evelyn (privacy) and Jordan (legal) to confirm the stop-gap controls and whether SLA credits apply. Proposed timeline: 48 hours for manifest + addendum draft; 72 hours for security scoping and recommendations. If that's too slow for your pilot, tell us and we'll accelerate.

Attachments: none in this message.

Best,

Kim / Jordan,

I've started a rapid assessment. Early findings and action items below:

Summary:
- EdgeProbe appears to operate hosted analytics collectors in SG and JP; current vendor profile shows TLS in transit and AES-256 at rest.
- No evidence in their public docs of EU-only residency for data; default assumption is cross-border transfer.

Immediate asks for the pilot to proceed:
1) KMS/HSM key management details: who holds keys for telemetry at rest? (EdgeProbe or customer-managed?)
2) Clarify whether the pilot will include any session identifiers or hashed IDs (hashing alone isn't sufficient without salt management).
3) Provide the minimal routing diagram (we need a simple egress map). Attached is an annotated diagram template to fill out.

Controls we will require for 30-day pilot:
- Pseudonymization of identifiers with customer-provided salt stored in the EU
- Explicit DPA addendum signed by both parties with subprocessor clause and SCCs (if needed)
- Canary rollout limited to 2% of traffic, with realtime error/latency alerting to both parties

Attachments: egress-diagram-annotated.pdf (template), processor-scoping-checklist.xlsx

I'll draft a short recommendation note for Legal once Kimberly confirms the data types. Jordan, if you see any contractual blockers for SLA credits or exceptions, flag them.

Cheers,
Evelyn Hart
Privacy Lead, Redwood Inference

Hi Olivia — attaching the manifest and a draft DPA addendum for your review (see attachments). Summary and proposed plan:

What we're sending you today:
- Full subprocessor manifest (attached: subprocessor_manifest_v2.csv).
- Draft DPA addendum that scopes EdgeProbe to telemetry-only processing and includes SCCs and standard transfer safeguards (attached: dpa-addendum-draft.docx).
- Annotated egress diagram (for clarity) and our scoping checklist (attached in prior thread).

Proposed pilot guardrails (we can put these into the addendum):
1) Canary: 2% traffic to EdgeProbe for 30 days. Immediate rollback on any error/latency spike > 200ms on avg token delivery to downstream features.
2) Data minimization: only anonymized metrics and timing data; no user identifiers unless pseudonymized with EU salt controlled by FinServe.
3) Key management: if EdgeProbe holds keys, we require explicit encryption-at-rest details; preferred is customer-managed keys (we can add KMS binding language into the addendum).
4) SLA compensation: if routing via EdgeProbe causes a sustained latency degradation that impacts a Redwood SLA route, we will offer a pro-rated credit tied to the incremental error rate — Jordan will propose language.

Next steps:
- Olivia: confirm data types and domain sample by EOD today so we can finalize addendum.
- FinServe Legal: review the attached draft and the proposed SLA clause.
- We will create a HubSpot ticket and a short Drive folder (links below) for artifacts.
